source1: Rudi Matthee & Hiroyuki Mashita, 'Kandahar iv. From the Mongol Invasion through the Safavid Era', Encyclopaedia Iranica - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/kandahar-from-the-mongol-invasion-through-the-safavid-era

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Zagwe dynasty' and 'Ethiopia: The Zagwe and Solomonic dynasties' - https://www.britannica.com/topic/Zagwe-dynasty ; https://www.britannica.com/place/Ethiopia/The-Zagwe-and-Solomonic-dynasties
source2: T. P. Ofcansky & L. Berry (eds), Ethiopia: A Country Study, 'The Restoration of the Solomonic Line', Library of Congress, 1991 - http://countrystudies.us/ethiopia/8.htm
notes: c.1270 Yekuno Amlak, Amhara/Shewan noble (internal rebel), killed Zagwe king Yitbarek and defeated a counter-rebellion, founding Solomonic line; centre shifted from Lasta to Amhara/Shewa. External-conquest reading (T2) possible if Amhara lay outside Zagwe control.

source1: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Aq Qoyunlu' - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/aq-qoyunlu-confederation ; with Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Esmail I Safawi i. Biography' - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/esmail-i-safawi/esma%ca%bfil-i-%e1%b9%a3afawi-i-biography/
notes: Post-1490 succession wars split the realm. Esmail, based in Gilan with Turkmen levies from Erzincan, beat Alvand at Sharur, took Tabriz 1501, Iraq-e Ajam/Fars 1503; remnants to 1508. Safavids' Ardabil origin makes 'external' debatable.

source1: Ouyang Xiu et al., Xin Tang shu, juan 219 (Shiwei section), 1060 - https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/%E6%96%B0%E5%94%90%E6%9B%B8/%E5%8D%B7219

source1: Department of Asian Art, 'Shang and Zhou Dynasties: The Bronze Age of China', Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History, Metropolitan Museum of Art - https://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/shzh/hd_shzh.htm
notes: Zhou, a western polity based near Xi'an (Wei valley), led a coalition that defeated the last Shang king c.1046 BCE and took over the Anyang region. Zhou's prior vassal status uncertain; treated as external.

source1: Pierre Leriche, 'Bactria i. Pre-Islamic Period', Encyclopaedia Iranica - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/bactria/bactria-i-pre-islamic-period/
notes: Ai Khanoum pillaged c.147; Eucratides-Euthydemid wars weakened kingdom; nomads (Yuezhi/Tochari) made Bactrians tributaries by 128 BCE and occupied Bactria; Zhang Qian found no supreme chief. Indo-Greek kingdoms persisted south of Hindu Kush.
